svg.title: Event-Driven vs. Scheduled Batch: The Decision Path
svg.desc: A root question asks whether the business must react within seconds of an event. If no, the path leads to a scheduled/interval pipeline. If yes, a second question asks whether the event itself is durable state that must be retained, branching to an event-driven pattern with a durable Eventhouse cold path versus a lightweight Activator-only notification pattern. A third question on the durable branch asks whether replay is required, branching to an idempotent replay design versus a simple durable log with no replay contract.
svg.text: Choose by reaction time, durable-state semantics, and recovery contract — not by novelty

g.aria-label: Must the business react within seconds?
g.title: Must the business react within seconds? — The root question: reaction-time requirement.
g.text: Must the business react within seconds?
Measure the required action latency — not source arrival frequency.

g.aria-label: Use a scheduled or interval pipeline
g.title: Use a scheduled or interval pipeline — Minutes-to-hours latency is fine — a Data Factory pipeline schedule covers it.

g.aria-label: Is the event durable business state?
g.title: Is the event durable business state? — Second question: must the event be retained and queried later, or is it just a trigger?
g.text: Must the event be retained and queried later?
A notification can be transient; a business fact needs durable history.
Evaluate and act; no analytical cold path

g.title: Activator-only notification pattern — Lightweight: evaluate and act, no durable cold-path storage.
g.text: Condition → action, no durable cold path
WARNING · A FIRED NOTIFICATION IS NOT RETAINED BUSINESS STATE

g.aria-label: Full event-driven pattern with Eventhouse cold path
g.title: Full event-driven pattern with Eventhouse cold path — Hot path for immediate action plus a durable Eventhouse/OneLake cold path.

g.aria-label: Is replay of failed/delayed events required?
g.title: Is replay of failed/delayed events required? — Third question, on the durable branch: does the design need a replay contract?
Idempotent replay + dead-letter design — Add an explicit idempotency key and dead-letter/replay procedure.
g.text: Stable idempotency key · dead-letter queue · resubmit via Real-Time hub

g.aria-label: Durable log with no replay contract
g.title: Durable log, no replay contract — Land the durable history but do not build a formal replay path.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset; item icons vendored under Microsoft's Fabric icon terms.
